$$Component_Title: A human readable name for the component.
$$Component_Description: A description of the component including information about its function.
$$Component_Type: A category describing the purpose of the component. ALLOWED VALUES interconnection:software:hardware:service:physical:process-procedure:plan:guidance:standard:validation
$$Rule_Id: A textual label that uniquely identifies a policy (desired state) that can be used to reference it elsewhere in this or other documents.
$$Rule_Description: A description of the policy (desired state) including information about its purpose and scope.
$$Profile_Source: A URL reference to the source catalog or profile for which this component is implementing controls for.
$$Profile_Description: A description of the profile.
$$Control_Id_List: A list of textual labels that uniquely identify the controls or statements that the component implements.
$$Namespace: A namespace qualifying the property's name.
$Parameter_Id: A textual label that uniquely identifies the parameter associated with that policy (desired state).
$Parameter_Description: A description of the parameter including the purpose and use of the parameter.
$Parameter_Value_Alternatives: ONLY for the policy (desired state) parameters: A value or set of values the parameter can take.
$Parameter_Value_Default: A value recommended by Compliance Team in this profile for the parameter.
$Check_Id: A textual label that uniquely identifies a check of the policy (desired state).
$Check_Description: A description of the check of the policy (desired state) including the method (interview or examine or test) and procedure details.
$Parameter_Id_2: A textual label that uniquely identifies a second parameter associated with that policy (desired state). Additional parameters are declared by repeating the four parameter columns with a common suffix.
$Parameter_Description_2: A description of the second parameter including the purpose and use of the parameter.
$Parameter_Value_Alternatives_2: ONLY for the policy (desired state) parameters: A value or set of values the second parameter can take.
$Parameter_Value_Default_2: A value recommended by Compliance Team in this profile for the second parameter.

$$Component_Description: Container image supply chain for the storefront stack: build provenance cosign signature verification and the cluster-held approved-registry ledger
$$Rule_Description: Every container image admitted into the storefront namespace carries a valid Sigstore/cosign signature made either by the approved release identity or by the organization's own signing key; verification happens at admission against the registry and (for the release identity) the Rekor transparency log. CM-14 Signed Components is the narrative control but is selected by no 800-53 rev5 baseline so SI-7(15) Code Authentication carries the mapping
$$Profile_Description: NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 HIGH baseline (KubeCon three-tier demo subset)
$Parameter_Description: OIDC subject of the release workflow permitted to sign storefront images (Sigstore keyless)
$Parameter_Description_2: OIDC issuer that must have asserted the signing identity. Paired with approved_signer_identity: a subject is only meaningful against the issuer that vouched for it, so both are authored here rather than one being fixed in the template

$$Component_Description: Container image supply chain for the storefront stack: build provenance cosign signature verification and the cluster-held approved-registry ledger
$$Rule_Description: Every container image is pulled from a registry that has an entry in the cluster-held approved-registry ledger (one ConfigMap per registry labelled supply-chain.example.com/ledger=approved-registry). The allow-list is cluster state and changes without redeploying policy
$$Profile_Description: NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 HIGH baseline (KubeCon three-tier demo subset)
$Parameter_Description: Namespace holding the approved-registry ledger ConfigMaps that the engine reads at evaluation time

$$Component_Description: Container image supply chain for the storefront stack: build provenance cosign signature verification and the cluster-held approved-registry ledger
$$Rule_Description: Every container image is referenced by immutable digest and never by a mutable tag such as latest so that the deployed baseline configuration is reproducible and the verified signature stays bound to the bytes that run
$$Profile_Description: NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 HIGH baseline (KubeCon three-tier demo subset)

$$Component_Description: Hand-rolled three-tier storefront on vanilla Kubernetes: web tier / api tier / db tier in namespace storefront
$$Rule_Description: No storefront container runs privileged or may escalate privileges; all Linux capabilities are dropped; runAsNonRoot is set; host namespaces and hostPath volumes are not used so that every workload keeps a separate execution domain
$$Profile_Description: NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 HIGH baseline (KubeCon three-tier demo subset)

$$Component_Description: Hand-rolled three-tier storefront on vanilla Kubernetes: web tier / api tier / db tier in namespace storefront
$$Rule_Description: Every storefront workload carries the inventory labels that make it attributable in the system component inventory: application name / part-of / data classification / owning team
$$Profile_Description: NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 HIGH baseline (KubeCon three-tier demo subset)
$Parameter_Description: Label keys every storefront workload must carry (blank separated). Rendered into a CEL list literal in all three engines

$$Component_Description: Hand-rolled three-tier storefront on vanilla Kubernetes: web tier / api tier / db tier in namespace storefront
$$Rule_Description: Database credentials reach the db and api tiers only through secretKeyRef; no credential environment variable may carry a literal value in the workload manifest where it would be exposed in etcd / kubectl output / Git / audit records
$$Profile_Description: NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 HIGH baseline (KubeCon three-tier demo subset)
$Parameter_Description: Environment variable names that must be sourced from a Secret rather than a literal value (blank separated)
